solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A spice very quietly eaten by noble

indicators.note: being eaten by something means sitting inside it, so the quiet letters go within the noble

parts.note: a noble is a peer of the realm
PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: A seasoning disappearing down the throat of an aristocrat at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepper is a common spice, ground from dried peppercorns.

clue.text: Young dog without tail starts to exasperate toy poodle

indicators.note: losing its tail means the final letter of the young dog's word is dropped

parts.note: a young dog is a puppy

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words give their opening letters

explanation.surface: A puppy ruining a toy poodle's patience, all dog-show chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poodle' looks like part of the dog picture, but it is the definition: in British usage a poodle is a servile follower who does another's bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone controlled by another, a lackey whose strings are pulled by a more powerful figure.

clue.text: Photo on a steamship: old painter

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

explanation.surface: A snapshot taken aboard a steamer, captioned with the name of an old painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish modern artist, is among the most famous painters of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Regularly need farm for dairy product

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dairy product naturally requires a farm to produce it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese, and cheese is a dairy product.

clue.text: Law, say, that's misused on every occasion

indicators.note: letters misused are put to the wrong order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that the law is abused every single time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on every occasion means doing it at all times, without exception.

clue.text: Golfer upset about a putt at first in game

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the next pieces
upset means knocked over, so the golfer's letters are rearranged
at first takes only the opening letter of putt

explanation.surface: A golfer throwing a tantrum over a putt during a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GOLFER into LEFROG, and 'about' wraps those letters around A and the P from 'putt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game of vaulting over a crouching player's back.

clue.text: Notice that is at front of university for so long

indicators.note: at front of places the earlier pieces before the next one

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A notice posted at the university gates bidding farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewells: a French goodbye and an informal English one.

clue.text: Cast consuming rum of poor-quality

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast, as at a coconut shy
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Actors drinking cheap rum, a picture of a shabby production.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are badly made, cheap and inferior, which is to be of poor quality.

clue.text: Drink something unsatisfactory before energetic game

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a lemon is slang for a dud, something that turns out unsatisfactory
squash is a fast, energetic racket game

explanation.surface: Advice to have a disappointing drink before a vigorous game of sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemon squash is a British soft drink made from a concentrated cordial diluted with water.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fruit-flavoured soft drink, so a beverage in the general sense.

clue.text: Best to get rid of groundbreaking tool

parts.note: the pick of a bunch is the best of it
to axe something is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: A recommendation that the best move is to scrap an innovative piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groundbreaking' reads as innovative, but here it means literally breaking the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickaxe is a heavy tool with a pointed head used to break up hard ground.

clue.text: In the morning I leave China

parts.note: a.m. marks the morning hours
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A traveller announcing a morning departure from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are friendly words for a friend or pal, one Spanish, one rhyming slang.

clue.text: Comfort in endless rental agreements

indicators.note: endless means both ends are cut off the synonym for the rental agreements

parts.note: leases are rental agreements for property

explanation.surface: A tenant finding consolation in rolling rental contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort and to ease both mean to relieve pain or distress, and as nouns both mean a state of relief.

clue.text: Prisoner discovered puzzle

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A captured escapee becoming a mystery to the guards.
explanation.definitionFit: To puzzle someone is to baffle or bewilder them, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Extremely reliable eyesight needed for a change

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of reliable

parts.note: vision is eyesight

explanation.surface: A note that very dependable eyesight is a requirement for a change of job.
explanation.definitionFit: A revision is an alteration or amendment, a change made to something.

clue.text: Pants coming from dogs drinking small spirit

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: boxers are a breed of dog
a short is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Underwear emerging from dogs knocking back a drop of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British for underpants, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose men's underpants, which the British call pants.

clue.text: An author to like, possibly new

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A writer one might come to enjoy, perhaps a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: J R R Tolkien wrote The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Way Australian or New Zealander cut lines

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: cut means the soldier's word loses its last letter

parts.note: an Anzac is a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

explanation.surface: An Antipodean slicing through a passage of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Small island's football shirt

definitions.meaning: a Channel Island, the largest of the group off Normandy
a footballer's numbered top is called by this name

explanation.surface: The kit worn by a little island's football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is a Channel Island, and a jersey is a knitted top worn by football players.

clue.text: Expression in America for end of the line

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: An American phrase for where a railway line finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final station on a rail or bus route, where the line ends.

clue.text: Some clear honey a flower in Europe supplied

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Clear honey supplied from a flower somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom that bees visit, but it is something that flows: a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river of Switzerland and France, a flower in the crossword sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Run away from what may bite you, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a flea is a biting insect

explanation.surface: Advice to bolt from anything likely to give you a nip.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to escape from or leave something in a hurry.

clue.text: Rugby player runs into father

indicators.note: into places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rugby forward charging into his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a front-row forward in a rugby scrum.

clue.text: Biblical girl I make complaint about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to moan is to make a complaint

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a girl from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman in the Old Testament Book of Ruth, Ruth's mother-in-law.

clue.text: Raids made by soldiers in filthy places

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the filthy places

parts.note: sties, pigsties, are proverbially filthy places
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops making attacks on squalid hovels.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorties are sudden attacks or raids made by troops from a defensive position.

clue.text: Getting older, awful gag in English

indicators.note: awful letters are in a terrible state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian past their prime telling a terrible joke in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing means growing old, the process of advancing in years.

clue.text: Just about exercises in public

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: only means just, merely
PE, physical education, is school exercises

explanation.surface: A modest boast of just about working out where people can see.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly is doing it in public view, without concealment.
